shorts.title: Newfoundland Had No Moose, Now It Has Over 100,000
shorts.outro: On that island's roads, a moose never has to attack anyone. Doug drove there at night. Full video below.
shorts.end_card: DID DOUG SEE IT IN TIME?
shorts.description: People shipped a handful of moose to an island with no predator big enough to stop them, and the full episode shows what that did to Doug on Newfoundland's night roads.

shorts.title: Moose Feed Underwater Because Their Nostrils Seal Shut
shorts.hook: A moose can vanish completely under a lake. On purpose.
shorts.outro: Underwater, a moose ignores you. On a snowed-in railway, Doug and a moose shared one track with a train coming. It's linked below.
shorts.description: A moose can sink completely under a lake to graze while water pressure valves its nose shut, and the full episode reveals whether it moves for a train on a snowed-in railway.

shorts.title: Two Bull Moose Were Found Frozen in Ice, Antlers Locked
shorts.hook: Two bull moose were found frozen in ice, antlers locked.
shorts.outro: Doug's antlers were made of cardboard. The bull's were not. How that ended is in the full video below.
shorts.end_card: DID THE CARDBOARD ANTLERS FOOL HIM?
shorts.description: Rutting bulls lock antlers so hard that two were found frozen together in Alaskan ice, and the full episode shows how Doug's cardboard antlers fared against one.

shorts.title: That Drunk Moose in an Apple Tree Probably Wasn't Drunk
shorts.outro: That moose couldn't get down. The one standing at the end of Doug's freshly shoveled Anchorage path could. Full video below.
shorts.end_card: WHO GAVE UP THE PATH FIRST?
shorts.description: Researchers say moose are likely too big to get drunk on fermented apples, and the full episode reveals who gave up an Anchorage path first, Doug or the moose.
